solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Though mad, Mudd refusing to see analyst

indicators.note: something gone mad is crazed and disordered, so the setter's name and the following word are jumbled together

parts.note: the setter's pseudonym, taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The setter, though crazy, won't go and see a psychiatrist.
explanation.walkthrough: Mudd is the setter's own byline, so the surface is a joke at his expense; 'to see' is just a link. 'Though mad' asks for MUDD and REFUSING to be shuffled together.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of psychoanalysis is the archetypal analyst, so the person names a profession by its best-known practitioner.

clue.text: I start to see in the dark, showing awareness

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other: the first letter of the next word sits in the darkness

parts.note: the dark is night-time

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone claims they can begin to see in darkness, proving how perceptive they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' takes S from 'see', which 'in' puts inside NIGHT; I goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep perception or understanding of something, a kind of awareness.

clue.text: It's more usual, primarily, to form dew, say?

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so these letters are shaped into a new word

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of 'it is' without the apostrophe
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A question about what dew usually forms from, asked in a meteorological tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to form' rearranges ITS, MORE and U (the first letter of 'usual', signalled by 'primarily'). 'say' marks dew as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dew is a film of condensed water droplets, an example of dampness on surfaces.

clue.text: Requirement to manipulate, by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells the solver to go by how a word is pronounced, not how it is written

parts.note: to knead dough is to work and manipulate it with the hands

explanation.surface: A job requirement involving manipulation, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEAD, to work dough with the hands, is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A need is something necessary, a straightforward synonym for a requirement.

clue.text: If almost by magic, a record producer appears

indicators.note: by magic things are transformed, so the words before are conjured into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A music producer appears out of nowhere, nearly by sorcery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost by magic' reads as one idiom, but 'by' is part of the fodder IF ALMOST BY, rearranged under 'magic'. Fatboy Slim is the stage name of Norman Cook, a British DJ and record producer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatboy Slim is a famous English big-beat DJ and producer of hit records, an example of the job named.

clue.text: Look round state for cliff top home

indicators.note: one word wraps round another, so the abbreviation sits inside the word for looking

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Survey the area for a house on top of a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island is a US state; American state abbreviations are fair game in cryptics. 'cliff top home' reads as a house but means a bird's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyrie is the nest of an eagle or other bird of prey, usually built high on a crag.

clue.text: Brave to seek money, given rant from tyrant

parts.note: dough is slang for money

indicators.note: one word is taken from another, so the letters of the shorter are removed from the longer

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A courageous person goes after cash despite a despot's ranting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to seek' and 'given' are link words; 'from' signals removal of one word's letters from the other's, leaving the last two letters of the despot.
explanation.definitionFit: Doughty is an old-fashioned word for valiant and fearless, a synonym of brave.

clue.text: Last laugh's with this, perhaps?

parts.note: the last laugh is read literally as the final laugh before death, the kind of grim joke made on the scaffold

explanation.definitionFit: Grim, ironic humour about death recalls jokes made by people about to be hanged.

clue.text: Great Victorian series about Liberal in frilly drawers

indicators.note: one word goes about the rest, so the word for a series wraps everything after it

parts.note: a chain of events is a series

indicators.note: the abbreviation for the party goes inside the rearranged underwear
frills ruffle the letters of the word they decorate, so this word is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A distinguished Victorian man is pictured in ruffled underwear, an absurd image.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frilly' looks like decoration of the underwear but is the anagram signal; the shuffled underwear with the party letter inside makes RLESDARW, held inside by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: The naturalist who wrote On the Origin of Species is one of the towering figures of the Victorian era.

clue.text: Omen, a Victoria Beckham, cryptically?

parts.note: taken as written
she was Posh Spice in the Spice Girls, and U is the crossword word for posh or upper-class

explanation.surface: Is a former pop star a sign of things to come?
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Beckham was 'Posh Spice'; 'cryptically' invites writing posh as U, the old label for upper-class usage, giving A U SPICE.
explanation.definitionFit: An auspice is a sign or portent, from Roman augury by watching birds.

clue.text: By being ruthless, hour preserved

indicators.note: something preserved is kept inside, so the abbreviation is held within the word for harsh

parts.note: being tough is being hard and ruthless

explanation.surface: A harsh manager keeps the time protected.
explanation.walkthrough: The one-word definition 'By' hides at the start, disguised as a preposition introducing the rest of the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Through and by both mean by way of or by means of, as in 'achieved through effort'.

clue.text: Insubstantial match

definitions.meaning: a match is used to ... a fire, as in 'have you got a ...?'

explanation.definitionFit: The answer means not heavy, and a request for a light asks for a match or lighter.

clue.text: Appearing as a couple, having to understand woman

parts.note: to get a joke is to understand it
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Two people seen as a pair, one needing to understand the woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people seen together are appearing in each other's company, as a couple would.

clue.text: To develop lifts, secure urban building

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting a word turns it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a storm that brews is developing
to lock something is to secure it

explanation.surface: A developer installs lifts and secures a building in the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' looks like elevators in a tall building, but it turns BREW upwards in this down clue to give WERB.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower block is a tall multi-storey residential or office building, typical of cities.

clue.text: Artist gets to spray theatre

parts.note: to water plants is to spray them
a theatre is a playhouse, and its audience is the house

explanation.surface: A painter spray-paints a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets to' is a link. John William Waterhouse was an English Pre-Raphaelite painter.
explanation.definitionFit: J. W. Waterhouse painted The Lady of Shalott, so the surname names a painter.

clue.text: Pumped-up Lebanese city?

parts.note: an ancient Phoenician port in southern Lebanon whose name sounds and is spelt like a wheel's inflated rubber ring

explanation.definitionFit: The Lebanese port shares its spelling with the inflated rubber cover on a car wheel, which is pumped up.

clue.text: Scold, married, punching handsome youth hard

indicators.note: punching into something gets inside it, so the abbreviation goes into the youth

parts.note: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite
H stands for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A married person scolds by thumping a good-looking young man hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punching' puts M inside ADONIS, and H follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish someone is to reprimand them firmly, a synonym of scold.

clue.text: Edge on top of plant pot

parts.note: a hem is the edge of a piece of cloth

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rim on top of a flowerpot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant pot' reads as one container, but 'plant' gives P and 'pot' is the definition; 'on' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, and the plant cannabis is also called by this name.

clue.text: King working in spring

indicators.note: one piece sits inside another, the word for working inside the month

parts.note: March is a spring month
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A king working during the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests a coiled spring or leaping, but names a month of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign ruler, and a king is one example.

clue.text: From which one might snigger, when late?

definitions.meaning: people snigger from behind a hand raised to hide their mouths

explanation.definitionFit: The word means behind time or in arrears, and the phrase split in two is where a snigger is hidden.

clue.text: Fire an individual with final move in board meeting?

parts.note: taken as written
I is one, a single individual
checkmate ends a game on a chessboard, so the final move in a board meeting is mate

explanation.surface: A boardroom question: sack someone as the last act of the meeting?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' and 'board meeting' suggest dismissal in a company, but fire means enliven and the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up is to enliven them, which is what animate means as a verb.

clue.text: Canadian province putting one past bloke, to a degree

indicators.note: one piece is placed past, that is after, the other

parts.note: a bloke is a man
I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A Canadian province advancing a single person beyond some fellow by degrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting one past bloke' places I after MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The province with Winnipeg as its capital is one of Canada's prairie provinces.

clue.text: Cutting through rodent, a long claw

indicators.note: the answer cuts across the boundaries of the words that follow, lying inside them

explanation.surface: A long claw tears into a rat or mouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'rodent' through 'a' into 'long'.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Cider drinker's heading behind willow

indicators.note: the heading, the front letter, goes behind, moving to the end of the name

parts.note: Rosie, from Laurie Lee's memoir Cider with Rosie, shares cider with the narrator

explanation.surface: A cider drinker's head lies behind a willow tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Cider with Rosie is Laurie Lee's memoir of an English country childhood. 'heading behind' moves the R of ROSIE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: An osier is a kind of willow whose pliant shoots are used for basket-making.

clue.text: African upland

definitions.meaning: a member of the Muslim people of north-west Africa
an open stretch of high uncultivated ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a North African Berber or Arab, and an expanse of high heathland such as Dartmoor.

clue.text: Painter possibly out to capture stream

indicators.note: to capture is to hold inside, so the rearranged word holds the stream
possibly signals one possible arrangement of the letters before it

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A painter might go outdoors to paint a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' gives UTO from the rearranged word. Maurice Utrillo painted Montmartre street scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French painter known for Paris street scenes, so his surname names a painter.

clue.text: Wise guys in press almost turning it around, but folding

indicators.note: the whole construction is turned around, read from end to start
the wise men go inside the shortened word for press
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is cut off

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
the Magi were the three wise men of the Nativity

explanation.surface: Three wise men press something, nearly turn it round, but end up folding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the last letter to give IRO; the wise men go inside to make IMAGIRO, and 'turning it around' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Principal follows daughter in long piece of cloth

indicators.note: one piece follows, coming after the other
the abbreviation sits inside the word for long

parts.note: to long for something is to hanker after it
chief means principal or main

explanation.surface: The head of a household follows a daughter wearing a long length of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like an adjective describing the cloth but is a verb, meaning to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A handkerchief is a small square of cloth used for wiping the nose.
